options.text: The absorption of heat by a dark surface
The transfer of heat by electromagnetic waves
The transfer of heat by the movement of a fluid
The transfer of thermal energy through a material by particle vibrations

questions.explanation: Thermal conduction is the transfer of thermal energy through a material by the vibration and collision of particles, without the material itself moving.

questions.stem: Why are metals good thermal conductors?

options.text: Because they have free electrons that transfer energy quickly
Because they have weak bonds between atoms

questions.explanation: Metals have free electrons that move rapidly through the structure, carrying energy from hot regions to cold regions much faster than particle vibrations alone.

questions.stem: In which state of matter is conduction most effective?

options.text: Conduction is equally effective in all states

questions.explanation: Conduction is most effective in solids, especially metals, because particles are closely packed and can transfer vibrations efficiently to neighbours.

questions.stem: Which of these materials would be the best thermal insulator?
questions.explanation: Wool is a good thermal insulator because it traps pockets of air. Air is a poor conductor, and the trapped air prevents convection, reducing heat transfer.

options.text: Particles vibrating and passing energy to neighbouring particles
Free electrons moving through the material

questions.explanation: In non-metals, there are no free electrons. Energy is transferred only by particles vibrating and colliding with their neighbours, which is a slower process.

questions.stem: A metal saucepan has a plastic handle. Why?

options.text: Plastic is a poor conductor, so the handle stays cool

questions.explanation: Plastic is a poor thermal conductor (a good insulator), so it does not transfer heat from the hot pan to your hand, keeping the handle cool enough to touch.

questions.stem: Which factor does NOT affect the rate of conduction through a material?

options.text: The thermal conductivity of the material
The temperature difference across the material

questions.explanation: The rate of conduction depends on temperature difference, cross-sectional area, thickness, and the material's thermal conductivity -- but not its colour. Colour affects radiation, not conduction.
